title: Regional traffic spiral mitigation and warmcache handoff scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is an on-call / post-incident scratchpad capturing operator steps, telemetry checks, and mitigation strategies for a region-level traffic spiral we saw during a partial-egress degradation. The goal is to capture the quick checks that helped stabilize traffic shifts and a proposed concise runbook we can add to the canonical failover playbook.

Context summary (incident snapshot):
- Date/time window: 2025-02-12 22:18 UTC -> 2025-02-13 01:05 UTC (primary spike period).
- Affected region: eu-west-3 (edge+ingress cluster degradation + intermittent egress throttling at cloud-provider egress layer).
- Observable effects: increased request latencies through eu-west-3 edge cluster, TTL-driven DNS queries bounced between edge nodes (client resolvers re-resolving), and gradual reweighting by traffic router produced a traffic spiral back into eu-west-3 despite capacity issues.
- Primary mitigations applied this run: manual per-region egress-quarantine (soft egress blackhole), immediate reduction of node weight in routing control plane, KV-cache preseed to warm standby in eu-central-1, and temporary DNS TTL override for critical zones.

What worked quickly:
- KV-preseed to warm standby reduced tail latencies for requests that hit cacheable prefixes: preseed command sequence below was executed in ~8 minutes and dropped tail from 3.6s -> 1.1s for cached traffic.
- Manual routing weight change (routerctl set-weight eu-west-3 0.15) prevented complete saturation while autoscale started.
- Short-term DNS TTL override to 30s (from 300s) for routing CNAMEs prevented long client pinning to failing endpoints; helped spread new client lookups to healthy regions.

What did NOT work / surprising behavior:
- DNS TTL oscillation: some downstream resolvers ignored short TTLs and cached the failing address, causing a minority of heavy clients to keep hitting eu-west-3 for tens of minutes.
- Auto-routing fallback policy saw a feedback loop: as weight dropped eu-west-3, backend health probes timed out due to cross-region egress issues, which then signaled router to re-increase weight (we need to decouple probe signal thresholds during degraded egress).
- KV cache preseed: initial keyset was missing high-cardinality prefixes for interactive chat sessions; op had to re-run a targeted prefix extract.

Operator checklist (short actionable run sequence for first responder):
1) Confirm region symptoms: run quick queries 
   - telemetry: sum(requests{region="eu-west-3"} by status) over last 5m
   - p50/p95/p99 latencies for routes: series query
2) If latency spike + increasing error rate, reduce router weight: routerctl set-weight <region> 0.10 (aim for 10% of normal)
3) If egress errors present, set egress quarantine: infractl egress-quarantine --region eu-west-3 --reason "operator-evac" --duration 30m
4) Trigger KV preseed to warm standby region: kvtool preseed --from eu-west-3 --to eu-central-1 --prefix-list /ops/preseed-critical-prefixes.txt --concurrency 8
   - Monitor preseed progress: kvtool status --job <id>
5) Shorten DNS TTL as stopgap (target 30s) for routing CNAMEs: dnsctl set-ttl routing-prod 30 --regions eu-*
6) Pause auto-router rollup for eu-west-3: routerctl suspend-auto-rollout --region eu-west-3 --until 2025-02-13T02:00:00Z
7) If auto-probes are making the router flip-flop, set probe override: routerctl set-probe-thresholds --region eu-west-3 --healthy-count 3 --grace-period 120s
8) Notify on-call SRE+networking and escalate to oncall infra if egress shows provider-level errors.

Quick commands and example outputs (for copy-paste):
- router weight: 
  > routerctl get-weights --region eu-west-3
  eu-west-3: 0.85
  > routerctl set-weight eu-west-3 0.10
  OK weight queued
- kv preseed: 
  > kvtool preseed --from eu-west-3 --to eu-central-1 --prefix-list /ops/preseed-critical-prefixes.txt --concurrency 8
  Job ID: preseed-20250212-435
  Progress: 40% (approx 6m remaining)
- dns: 
  > dnsctl set-ttl routing-prod 30 --regions eu-*
  OK updated 5 records

Telemetry checks & dashboards to open (minimal set):
- SRE -> regional-egress -> egress-errors-by-node (last 15m)
- Platform -> routing -> weights-and-decision-log (show last 60 decisions)
- Serving -> kvcache -> preseed-jobs
- Edge -> resolver-errors -> client-ttl-breakdown

Timeline (operator-annotated):
- 22:18 UTC: first tail latency increase in eu-west-3, alert P0 triggered (latency p99>2s)
- 22:23 UTC: ops acknowledges, reduces router weight to 0.15
- 22:28 UTC: egress quarantine issued after provider error spikes observed
- 22:36 UTC: KV preseed job started to eu-central-1
- 22:45 UTC: DNS TTL shortened to 30s for routing records
- 23:02 UTC: partial improvement in request distribution; some clients still hitting eu-west-3 due to resolver caching
- 00:15 UTC: provider acknowledged egress issue; egress errors decreased
- 01:05 UTC: region returned to normal and weights restored gradually to 0.85 -> 1.0 over 30m with staged rollouts

Root cause hypotheses and followups (investigation action items):
- Hypothesis A: Provider-level egress throttling causing increased retransmits and probe failures -> leads router to misinterpret transient health.
  Action: open ticket with provider (INF-2317), attach pcap/egress error traces, ask for root cause and whether they did internal traffic shaping at 22:20-22:50 UTC. Owner: Marco Chen. Target: 2025-03-05.
- Hypothesis B: Router health probe sensitivity too aggressive in presence of high tail latencies -> creates flip-flop when traffic is reweighted.
  Action: add safe mode in router to treat egress errors as throttling and require N consecutive failures from distinct egress nodes before weight increase. Owner: SRE team. Target: 2025-03-12.
- Hypothesis C: Downstream resolvers ignoring TTLs and caching failing endpoints -> long tail of bad clients.
  Action: investigate client IP list and resolver behavior, create list of top resolvers (ASNs) that ignored TTLs, add resolver-level mitigation guide. Owner: Lena Ortiz. Target: 2025-03-08.

Temporary mitigations to standardize (proposals):
- Add a routing-safemode flag for egress degradation: when set, routing will move traffic away based on aggregate egress error rate, not short-lived probe flaps. (Design doc pending).
- Make KV preseed prefix extraction automated for top-200 prefixes by QPS; precompute a daily delta snapshot to speed targeted reseeds.
- Add an operator-facing "force-dns-refresh" endpoint that triggers a propagated CNAME change (with low TTL) for critical routing buckets to reduce client pinning.

Outstanding questions / risks:
- TTL reduction side-effects: will spiky resolver queries create a temporary load on DNS infra? (we saw +70% queries for routing CNAMEs for 10 minutes).
- Will forced preseed increase cross-region egress costs and is that acceptable for 30m windows? Need cost swing estimate.
- Do we need a runbook section for ASR/large-enterprise customers whose resolvers have aggressive caching? How to coordinate?

Action items (short list):
- [ ] Create RFC for router safe-mode behavior (owner: Devon) by 2025-03-12.
- [ ] Automate top-prefix extraction for preseed (owner: Aisha) by 2025-03-20.
- [ ] Postmortem writeup (owner: Aisha) and link to INF-2317 by 2025-03-04.
- [ ] Provider ticket follow-up and artifact collection (owner: Marco) by 2025-03-05.
- [ ] Resolver analysis for TTL-ignoring clients (owner: Lena) by 2025-03-08.

Notes to self / operator heuristics (informal):
- If preseed job stalls > 10m, re-run with --concurrency 2 (less noisy) and a smaller prefix list.
- When reducing weight, avoid instant 0.0 unless evacuating; 0.1-0.2 helps keep warm caches valid.
- Use staging of DNS TTL rollbacks: set TTL low first, then a minute later change CNAME target. This pattern helped us in 2/12 run.

Appendix: quick lookups / queries used during incident:
- Prom: sum(rate(http_requests_total{region="eu-west-3"}[1m])) by (code)
- Prom: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{region="eu-west-3"}[5m])) by (le))
- KV: kvtool list-jobs --last 24h | grep preseed

Draft status: keep as scratchpad for 1 week, convert high-confidence items into canonical runbook and add to confluence page "regional-failover-operator-playbook".

End of scratchpad.
